messages:
release-coordinator: Kicking off staged rollout for release v2.14.0 -> starting 0% -> 5% canary now. Change window 2h. release notes: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RW-1421 :rocket:

deploy-bot: deploy started by release-coordinator at 2026-03-20T15:00:34Z. Rolling traffic to v2.14.0: 0% -> 5%. Canary pool: canary-gpu-2 (10 pods).

monitoring-bot: alert: p95 latency for /generate increased from 190ms -> 420ms over last 3m in canary region us-west-2. Error rate unchanged (0.3%). :eyes:

matt: seeing the same in traces, spans show a spike in kv-cache misses for generation calls. Could be cache key change from prompt normalization tweak.

sara: sending logs. snippet: ```2026-03-20T15:02:10Z ERROR kvcache miss key=prompt_norm_v1 user=svc-embedded```

priya: @release-coordinator i'd vote hold at 5% and investigate. small blast radius, we can pin back if needed. :thumbsup:

jin: +1 hold. can we pin traffic to v2.13.9 for affected customer buckets while we debug?

release-coordinator: Ok holding at 5% for 20m. no further increases. If we can't identify quick fix, rollback to v2.13.9 or pin by routing rule. Can someone run the pin command?

matt: running pin now: `redwoodctl routing set --model my-text-gen --version v2.13.9 --match-tags region:us-west-2`

deploy-bot: routing change submitted by matt. Action ID: act-7782. Routing broadcast: pinned my-text-gen -> v2.13.9 for region=us-west-2 (canary pool).

ops-bot: infra note: canary pods scaled back to 0 for v2.14.0 in us-west-2. No extra infra churn.

monitoring-bot: update: p95 back down to 210ms in canary region after pin applied (2m). :tada:

priya: nice. still want to root cause the kv-cache key change before unpausing. who owns that prompt normalization change?

matt: that was me — PR #2483 changed whitespace normalization for better LLM alignment. I'll revert the normalization in a hotfix branch and run a canary local.

release-coordinator: plan: 1) hold traffic at 5% (done). 2) matt will ship hotfix to revert normalization and create a patch v2.14.1. 3) re-run canary in a controlled 5% -> 10% ramp after monitoring stability for 10m. 4) if any regression, rollback to v2.13.9 and file postmortem. Agreed?

jin: agreed. please add the rollback trigger thresholds to the thread (p95 > 300ms sustained 5m or error rate >1%).

release-coordinator: added thresholds. Also noting change window ends 17:00 UTC. If we don't clear by 16:30 UTC we rollback to reduce exposure.

matt: pushing hotfix now, CI queued. build 2589 -> image sha: sha256:9f2a... deploy to canary after successful e2e.

deploy-bot: automated canary deploy queued: build=2589 -> awaiting manual approval for resume.

priya: i'm on standby for approvals. once monitoring-bot shows stable for 10m, i'll approve a cautious ramp to 10%.

monitoring-bot: note: synthetic traffic for critical flow shows no functional errors, only latency hit which resolved after pin. continuing 10m observation.

release-coordinator: thanks all. leaving this thread pinned. If anyone needs to escalate, call page on-call SRE. :phone:

matt: quick note for release notes: adding rollback instructions and pinning commands to the doc. link updated.

jin: +1 thanks. will prepare a short ops blurb for customers in case rollback occurs.

deploy-bot: user=release-coordinator paused automatic ramp at 5% (act-7782). To resume: `deploy-bot resume act-7782` or approve via console.

priya: approving resume only after monitoring shows 10m of stability post-hotfix. will post here when i click approve.

monitoring-bot: 10m window started at 2026-03-20T15:07:34Z. Current p95=205ms, errors=0.28%.

last: release-coordinator: holding until approx 15:30 UTC for outcome, otherwise rollback scheduled at 16:30 UTC. Thanks team. :pray:
